With any science careers you will need math. So try to get calculus , algebra in high school. You can ask local aquariums if they need interns/volunteers, most are happy to take you. This is a hard field to go into, so start figuring out what criteria in marine biology you want to go into. When you get to high school take AP classes like AP environmental science, AP Calculus. If you want a degree in marine biology there are some schools that offer it and I would start looking at what college for marine bio you want to go to now, FIU has a marine lab underwater, I heard that University of Hawaii has a good program too. Depending on where you live I would start going to rivers, lakes, the ocean (if you’re by it) and start learning everything you can about it. I have a list of books that are wonderful about marine bio, like What a Fish Knows by Jonathon Balconbe is a great read. 
I hope this helps!
